question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse tool execution mode in core, and should that wait for explicit tool concurrency-safety metadata before any early execution is allowed?
rationale: The source-level opportunity is real, but the change alters core runtime semantics and safety policy rather than fixing a narrowly broken existing contract.

options.title: Design opt-in core mode
options.body: Keep this issue open for a core design covering streaming dispatch, safety metadata, transcript ordering, approvals, cancellation, hooks, and regression proof.

options.title: Block on safety metadata
options.body: Treat this as dependent on the tool-classification work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62962 or an equivalent concurrency contract.

options.title: Keep post-stream batching only
options.body: Decline early execution for now if maintainers decide the latency gain is not worth the runtime and safety complexity.

recommendation.title: Design opt-in core mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a core design covering streaming dispatch, safety metadata, transcript ordering, approvals, cancellation, hooks, and regression proof.
